article.api.text01: MineCore has an event-driven API. Use MineCoreApi to access managers and the event bus, and connect your server logic through Bukkit events.
article.api.text03: The singleton instance is the entry point to the API:
article.api.text06: The request manager can fetch, create, accept and cancel requests, and accept or reject votes:
article.api.text08: MineCorePreCreateRequestEvent is cancellable and contains the request being created.
article.api.text09: MineCorePostCreateRequestEvent contains the created request and its ID.
article.api.text12: See also the event listener guide and Skript hooks.
article.fejlfinding.text02: This error usually means the JAR was built for a newer Java version than the server's JVM. Check java -version, then download or build MineCore for the same target.
article.fejlfinding.text04: Check your Skript version, Java version and console output during startup. MineCore downloads hooks to plugins/MineCore/hooks/ based on the detected version.
article.fejlfinding.text05: A vote or payment gives no reward
article.fejlfinding.text06: Check that the correct receive event is registered, the player's UUID can be found, and the request or vote is accepted after successful processing.
article.fejlfinding.text07: Report reproducible problems in MineCore issues, including your server version, Java version and relevant console output.
article.kom-i-gang.text01: MineCore lets you receive MineClub payments and votes directly on your server. Enable MineCore, select the appropriate Skript hook if you use Skript, and restart the server.
article.kom-i-gang.text03: Hosting your own server? Follow the Paper, Velocity and Waterfall setup guide. To register your server on MineClub, use the external server guide.
article.kom-i-gang.text04: Run this command in the server console or as a player with the required permissions:
article.kom-i-gang.text06: Restart the server after enabling or disabling MineCore for the change to take effect.
article.kom-i-gang.text08: A supported server version from Minecraft 1.8 to 26.2.
article.kom-i-gang.text09: A JVM version from Java 8 to Java 26.
article.kom-i-gang.text11: A Skript hook if you use Skript.
article.kom-i-gang.text13: MineCore supports Minecraft versions from 1.8 to 26.2 and JVM versions from JVM 8 to JVM 26. Always choose the MineCore variant that matches the Java version your server actually runs.
article.kom-i-gang.text14: If you use Skript, support depends on your server's Skript version. Use the matching Skript hook so that MineCore events, effects and expressions are registered correctly.
article.kom-i-gang.text15: Next, follow the installation guide to learn how to build your own plugin using MineCore.
article.skript.text01: MineCore provides hooks for Skript 2.2-dev36, 2.9.5, 2.13.2 and 2.15.3. The hook is selected automatically based on your Skript and Java versions.
article.skript.text05: Skript 2.13.2, 2.9.5 and 2.15.3 use the modern Section API. Skript 2.2-dev36 uses a legacy compatibility layer but supports the same basic request and vote effects.
article.guides.text01: These guides cover the integrations you will typically build on top of MineCore.
article.guides.text03: MineCore uses events to describe the full journey from building a request to creating it and receiving it on the server. Votes have their own receive flow.
article.guides.text10: PreCreateRequestEvent is sent with a StoreRequest before the request is created. Use the event to validate or stop a request that must not be sent.
article.guides.text11: If the event is cancelled, callEvent() returns true and the request should not continue.
article.guides.text13: PostCreateRequestEvent is sent when the request has been created. It provides a StoreCreatedRequest containing the created request's ID, which can be saved for later tracking.
article.guides.text14: 3. When the server receives a request
article.guides.text15: ReceiveRequestEvent means the server has received a request from MineClub. The event contains both a type and a StoreCreatedRequest. Use the type to distinguish requests, and grant the reward only after validating the request data.
article.guides.text16: Do not mark the reward as completed until your own processing has succeeded. This makes retries easier to handle without granting the same reward more than once.
article.guides.text18: The Skript hook uses the same four stages through Skript events. You can build the request, respond before and after creation, and finally handle the request or vote received by the server.
article.guides.text25: Use pre create request to check the request before it is sent. With a Skript hook that supports event cancellation, you can stop the flow using cancel event.
article.guides.text28: Use event-request and event-vote in accept effects to mark the current request or vote as processed. Always check your own rewards before accepting so retries cannot grant duplicate rewards.
article.guides.text29: 4. When the server receives a vote
article.guides.text30: ReceiveVoteEvent contains a MappedVote. Grant the player's vote reward, then call acceptVote. Use rejectVote if the vote data cannot be processed.
article.guides.text32: Event classes post themselves through MineCoreApi.getInstance().getAsyncEventBus().post(this). Treat handlers as asynchronous: avoid direct Bukkit or world operations in the event handler, and use the server scheduler when an action requires the main thread.
article.guides.text33: See the API reference for event fields and managers, or Skript hooks for the same lifecycle in Skript.
article.installation.text01: This guide shows how to build a Paper plugin with the MineCore Java API. It follows the structure of the MineCore repository's example module.
article.installation.text03: Your plugin needs a class extending JavaPlugin and a plugin.yml. The example uses ExamplePlugin as its entry point.
article.installation.text05: The example uses the Java 25 variant of the API. Choose the artifact matching your Java target.
article.installation.text06: The MineCore example uses Gradle Kotlin DSL in example/build.gradle.kts. It also enables the Shadow plugin to build the plugin JAR as a bundled distribution.
article.installation.text07: Make the MineCore API available at runtime. Either shade the API into your own plugin JAR using Shadow, or use MineCore as a separate plugin and declare it as a soft dependency.
article.installation.text08: If MineCore is provided separately on the server, the dependency can be compileOnly so the API is not bundled into your plugin again:
article.installation.text10: Create src/main/resources/plugin.yml and point main to your JavaPlugin class:
article.installation.text11: Add softdepend when MineCore is a separate plugin in the server's plugins/ directory:
article.installation.text12: Only use the softdepend model if the MineCore plugin is actually installed. If you shade the API into your own JAR, do not make your plugin depend on a separate MineCore installation.
article.installation.text14: The example creates an API instance in onEnable(), then registers event listeners on MineCore's asynchronous event bus.
article.installation.text16: The example's BuyCommand builds a StoreProduct, places it in a StoreRequest and sends the request through the request manager.
article.installation.text18: The MineCore Java API also supports server payments through RequestManager. A ServerPayRequest contains the player's Minecraft account as text in mcaccount and the amount in amount. Send it through createServerPay; the method returns a ServerPayResponse if the call succeeds.
article.installation.text19: The API serializes the request to JSON and sends it to /server/pay using the MineCore token. If the request is null, the response is missing, or the call fails, createServerPay returns null.
article.installation.text20: Always use ServerPayRequest and ServerPayResponse from the same API artifact as the rest of your plugin.
article.installation.text22: Fetch votes through RequestManager.getVotes. Use GetVotesOptions to filter by player, status, page and result count. GetVotesResponse.getAll() provides the vote list whether or not the response is paginated.
article.installation.text23: A MappedVote includes id, status, createdAt, updatedAt and mcaccount. After processing a received vote, mark it with acceptVote(vote). Use rejectVote(vote) if the vote data cannot be processed.
article.installation.text25: Register a class using Guava's @Subscribe. MineCore's example handles pre-create, post-create, received requests and votes in the same listener:
article.installation.text26: See the event lifecycle guide for the differences between events and when they are called.
article.installation.text28: Run the build from the MineCore project root using the Gradle wrapper:
article.installation.text30: Install the built JAR from example/build/libs/ into the Paper server's plugins/ directory, then restart the server. Use the same Java target for the API artifact, compilation target and server JVM.
article.installation.text31: The API example is based on MineCore's dev branch. Check the specific release before pinning the artifact and Paper API versions in your own plugin.

article.eksterne-servere.text01: An external server runs on your own hardware or with your hosting provider and is registered on MineClub. You manage the server files, updates, networking and starting or stopping it.
article.eksterne-servere.text02: Need to set up the server first? See the Paper, Velocity and Waterfall setup guide. That guide covers standalone servers and networks; connecting through MineClub requires the settings on this page.
article.eksterne-servere.text04: Log in to MineClub with the Minecraft account that will own the server. Run the command in-game with your chosen name:
article.eksterne-servere.text05: The name must be available and contain 3–16 letters. Danish letters are allowed; numbers, spaces and hyphens are not. Registration does not create a server with a hosting provider.
article.eksterne-servere.text06: 2. Save the connection in the panel or in-game
article.eksterne-servere.text10: Open the MineClub panel, select the owner's Minecraft account and external server, then open Settings.
article.eksterne-servere.text11: Under Connection, enter the server's IPv4 or IPv6 address and port. Use an IP address without a domain name, protocol or port in the IP field. The port must be an integer from 1 to 65535.
article.eksterne-servere.text12: Choose the forwarding protocol your server accepts and enter the Minecraft version it actually runs.
article.eksterne-servere.text13: Once the server is running with your provider and you are ready to test the connection, choose Online under Status on Mineclub.
article.eksterne-servere.text14: Click Save settings, then configure forwarding on your server as described below.
article.eksterne-servere.text16: You can also save the IP address and port using /sm set. These commands change your selected primary server, which must be an external server. First select the correct server with /sm changeserver and use tab completion for its name.
article.eksterne-servere.text17: Replace the placeholders with your own values, such as your server's IP address and port 25565. Include a space after set and spell externalIp and externalPort exactly as shown. Wait for confirmation of the server selection before changing the connection.
article.eksterne-servere.text18: Changes are saved immediately; changing the IP or port in-game also resets approval to Draft. Continue with forwarding and approval below.
article.eksterne-servere.text19: Once the server is running with your provider and ready for testing, set the selected external server to Online with:
article.eksterne-servere.text20: To mark it Offline again, use /sm set online false. The command is named online and accepts true or false.
article.eksterne-servere.text21: The address must be reachable from MineClub. Do not use 127.0.0.1 as an external address: it refers to the machine making the connection. Allow MineClub connections in your provider's network rules; ask MineClub for the current source addresses if you need an allowlist.
article.eksterne-servere.text22: Configure the firewall before testing or opening access: Block inbound TCP traffic from the internet to the external server's IP address and port, allowing only MineClub's trusted source addresses on that port. This prevents direct connections that bypass MineClub. Get the current addresses from MineClub and apply the rules to both IPv4 and IPv6 if both are available.
article.eksterne-servere.text23: Restrict inbound traffic from outside. Your Velocity or Waterfall proxy must still be able to make outbound HTTPS connections to api.mineclub.dk on TCP port 443 for login verification. Test that connecting through MineClub works and that direct access to the server's IP and port from another internet connection is blocked.
article.eksterne-servere.text24: Minecraft version changes the registration but does not install a new server version. Status on Mineclub must be Online to connect using /server. Changing this status does not start or stop the server process; manage that with your provider.
article.eksterne-servere.text26: External Velocity and Waterfall proxies can only connect to MineClub using HAProxy. Select HAProxy in the panel and enter the proxy's IP address and listening port. MODERN, LEGACY and BungeeGuard in the panel are for direct connections to a compatible backend such as Paper; they are not used between MineClub and your Velocity or Waterfall proxy.
article.eksterne-servere.text27: MODERN (Velocity): For Paper with modern forwarding support. After saving, the panel displays a Forwarding secret. Use it as proxies.velocity.secret in Paper's config/paper-global.yml.
article.eksterne-servere.text28: LEGACY (BungeeCord): The server must accept BungeeCord forwarding, for example with settings.bungeecord: true in Paper's spigot.yml. Restrict backend access to the trusted proxy.
article.eksterne-servere.text29: BungeeGuard: Requires legacy forwarding and BungeeGuard on the receiving server. Save the settings and add the panel's BungeeGuard token to the plugin's allowed tokens. Follow the BungeeGuard installation instructions.
article.eksterne-servere.text30: HAProxy: Choose this only if the receiver is configured for the PROXY protocol. This is a separate protocol and cannot be replaced by a Velocity secret or BungeeCord setting.
article.eksterne-servere.text31: For a direct connection from MineClub to Paper using modern forwarding, set online-mode=false in server.properties, set settings.bungeecord to false and enable Paper's Velocity support. Paper must use MineClub's secret, and the forwarding online-mode setting must match the authenticating proxy. See the file locations in the Paper configuration in the Velocity section.
article.eksterne-servere.text32: The panel's secret belongs to the connection from MineClub. A standalone Velocity network uses its own forwarding.secret. Do not mix these secrets or share them in screenshots, chat or public configuration files.
article.eksterne-servere.text33: If the secret field asks you to save, click Save settings to display the secret. Stop the server before changing files and start it again afterwards.
article.eksterne-servere.text37: Stop Velocity and add MineClub's session URL as a JVM argument before -jar. Adjust the JAR name to match your installed version:
article.eksterne-servere.text38: On the Velocity proxy — velocity.toml: Edit online-mode at the root and haproxy-protocol in the existing [advanced] section. Do not add another section or a comma after true.
article.eksterne-servere.text39: The HAProxy setting's location is documented in the Velocity configuration reference. The onward connection from your Velocity proxy to Paper still uses your own forwarding configuration, such as modern forwarding with the proxy's own forwarding.secret. See Velocity → Paper.
article.eksterne-servere.text41: Waterfall uses the JVM argument waterfall.auth.url. The URL must contain format placeholders for the username, server ID and optional IP parameter, as shown in Waterfall's official auth-url patch.
article.eksterne-servere.text42: Terminal — Waterfall proxy: Stop the proxy and start it with this command. Adjust the JAR name; keep the quotes around the JVM argument so the shell does not interpret &.
article.eksterne-servere.text43: Waterfall replaces the three %s placeholders. In a Windows .bat or .cmd file, double each percent sign so the URL portion becomes ?username=%%s&serverId=%%s%%s. Use ordinary %s in PowerShell and Linux/macOS terminals.
article.eksterne-servere.text44: On the Waterfall proxy — config.yml: Keep online_mode at the root and enable proxy_protocol on the existing listener MineClub connects to. Preserve its other settings.
article.eksterne-servere.text45: proxy_protocol is a listener setting in the BungeeCord configuration that Waterfall builds on. ip_forward: true applies to the separate onward connection to Paper and does not replace proxy_protocol. Keep the backend setup from Waterfall → Paper.
article.eksterne-servere.text46: HAProxy passes connection information; the session URL handles login verification. Both must be configured. Restrict the proxy's HAProxy port to MineClub's trusted source addresses and test by connecting through MineClub. A regular Minecraft client does not send the required PROXY header directly to this port.
article.eksterne-servere.text47: Restart the entire proxy process after changing JVM arguments or configuration. Then check login, the player's UUID and access to your Paper backend through MineClub. These instructions are based on configuration and source code; they are not a live test of your particular proxy build.
article.eksterne-servere.text49: Start the server with your provider and set its status to Online using /sm set online true or Settings → Status on Mineclub → Online → Save settings on the website. This also applies during testing.
article.eksterne-servere.text50: With a complete IP address and port, the owner can test access before approval; staff with the relevant access can also test. Check the connection, player identity and server log before submitting. A complete address alone does not prove the server is reachable.
article.eksterne-servere.text51: Online does not mean approved. Regular players can connect when the server is Online, has a valid connection and is approved (verified). Online status alone does not open a draft or rejected server to everyone.
article.eksterne-servere.text52: Save all changes and click Submit for approval under Approval in the panel. You can also submit it in-game from the owner's Minecraft account:
article.eksterne-servere.text53: View the status of your external servers and any explanation with:
article.eksterne-servere.text54: Draft (draft): Configure and test the server, then submit it for approval.
article.eksterne-servere.text55: Pending approval (pending): The server has been submitted. You cannot resubmit it while it is pending.
article.eksterne-servere.text56: Approved (verified): The server can be publicly accessible on MineClub when the owner and connection are valid. It must still be configured correctly and running with your provider.
article.eksterne-servere.text57: Rejected (rejected): Read the explanation, fix the problem, save and test. Choose Resubmit for approval or use the submit command.
article.eksterne-servere.text58: Changing the IP address or port resets approval to Draft. Test the new connection and submit the server again. This also applies to an already approved server.
article.eksterne-servere.text60: The button is disabled: Select the owner's Minecraft account, save changes and check the IP/port. Only draft and rejected servers can be submitted.
article.eksterne-servere.text61: The IP address is rejected: Use an IPv4 or IPv6 address, not a domain name. Enter the port in its separate field.
article.eksterne-servere.text62: The connection fails: Check the server process, listening port, firewall and forwarding. The displayed Online status does not start the server.
article.eksterne-servere.text63: Wrong secret or forwarding error: Match the panel's protocol and secret to the receiving server, then restart after changing files.
article.eksterne-servere.text64: The owner can connect but others cannot: Check approval status. The owner's test access does not mean the server is publicly approved.
article.eksterne-servere.text65: Status changed during submission: Refresh the panel and read the current status before trying again.
article.eksterne-servere.text66: Removing a server in the panel deletes its registration from MineClub. It does not delete the server or its files with your hosting provider.
article.serveropsaetning.text01: Choose one setup: standalone Paper, Velocity with Paper or Waterfall with Paper. The proxy examples use one machine with public port 25565 and a Paper backend at 127.0.0.1:25566.
article.serveropsaetning.text02: These are standalone networks that players connect to directly. To connect from MineClub to your Velocity or Waterfall proxy, use HAProxy and MineClub's session URL as described in Velocity through MineClub or Waterfall through MineClub. Settings for the onward connection to Paper are below.
article.serveropsaetning.text04: You need access to edit files, run Java and change your provider's network rules. Use separate directories for Paper and the proxy. Back up existing server files, stop processes before making changes and edit the existing keys in generated files. The examples are snippets to merge without duplicating YAML sections or TOML tables.
article.serveropsaetning.text05: Run this in a terminal on the server machine:
article.serveropsaetning.text06: Choose Java for your specific server release. PaperMC's Java overview recommends Java 21 for Paper 1.20–1.21.11 and Java 25 for 26.1+. The current Velocity guide requires Java 25. Older releases may have different requirements; check your release before installing.
article.serveropsaetning.text07: The startup commands work in terminals on Windows, Linux and macOS. Run them from the relevant directory, use the shown JAR names or adjust the filename, and adapt the memory allocation to your hosting plan.
article.serveropsaetning.text09: Download a suitable server release from Paper's official downloads, place it in the Paper directory and rename it to paper.jar.
article.serveropsaetning.text10: Run this command from the Paper directory to generate the server files.
article.serveropsaetning.text12: Read Minecraft's EULA using the link in eula.txt. If you accept it, change eula=false to eula=true. Start again with the same command, let the server generate the world, then enter stop in the console before changing configuration.
article.serveropsaetning.text14: Keep proxy support disabled for direct player access: settings.bungeecord: false in spigot.yml and proxies.velocity.enabled: false in config/paper-global.yml. See below for the older Paper file.
article.serveropsaetning.text15: Start Paper again. Allow TCP port 25565 in your firewall and router port forwarding if needed. Use your provider's assigned port if different. Connect using Minecraft Java Edition to the server's public address; on the same machine, you can use localhost:25565.
article.serveropsaetning.text16: Check: You should be able to log in with your normal Minecraft account and see the expected name and skin. Paper authenticates players itself with online-mode=true.
article.serveropsaetning.text18: The connection is player → Velocity:25565 → Paper:25566. Use modern forwarding with a compatible Paper release. First stop Paper from the previous section to free port 25565.
article.serveropsaetning.text20: Download Velocity to its own directory as velocity.jar. Run the command, then stop the proxy with end once its configuration has been created.
article.serveropsaetning.text22: Proxy machine — velocity.toml: Edit the root settings before the first table. Replace the example servers in [servers] with your lobby, and remove or adjust generated [forced-hosts] references to servers you do not use.
article.serveropsaetning.text24: Install Paper and generate its files as in the Paper section if you do not already have a server. Stop it before making changes.
article.serveropsaetning.text27: Paper machine — config/paper-global.yml: Replace the placeholder with the full contents of the proxy's generated forwarding.secret. Keep the secret private.
article.serveropsaetning.text28: The proxy authenticates the player, so online-mode is disabled in the backend's server.properties but enabled in the proxy and Paper's Velocity settings.
article.serveropsaetning.text29: Older Paper: On 1.18.2 and earlier, these settings are in paper.yml instead. Only use this snippet if your release uses the old file:
article.serveropsaetning.text30: Modern forwarding requires support in the server release and does not work with Minecraft versions below 1.13. See PaperMC's forwarding guide for compatibility and official file settings.
article.serveropsaetning.text32: Start Paper first, then Velocity using the commands above. Connect to the proxy's public address on port 25565. Check login, skin and the player's UUID in the backend log or an administration plugin against the account's normal online UUID. Also test backend access restrictions.
article.serveropsaetning.text34: PaperMC considers Waterfall discontinued. Use Velocity for new networks. This section is for existing Waterfall installations and requires Paper and client versions supported by your Waterfall build.
article.serveropsaetning.text36: Use Waterfall's official download page and check the Java requirement for your build in the installation guide. Place waterfall.jar in a separate directory. Stop other processes on port 25565, run the command and enter end once the files have been generated.
article.serveropsaetning.text38: Proxy machine — config.yml: Edit the existing listener and server list; preserve the other settings on your listener.
article.serveropsaetning.text39: Here, Waterfall receives ordinary client connections, so proxy_protocol is disabled. The server name in priorities must exist under servers. See the BungeeCord configuration reference for the shared settings.
article.serveropsaetning.text41: Generate the Paper files and accept the EULA as in the Paper section. Stop Paper and use the following backend settings.
article.serveropsaetning.text45: On Paper 1.18.2 and earlier, use settings.bungee-online-mode: true and settings.velocity-support.enabled: false in paper.yml. The proxy must still use online_mode: true.
article.serveropsaetning.text47: Start Paper, then Waterfall. Connect to the proxy's public address on port 25565 and check that you reach the lobby with your correct name, skin and online UUID. Legacy forwarding has no built-in shared secret, so also complete the network checks below.
article.serveropsaetning.text49: For proxy setups, expose only the proxy's TCP port 25565 to players. The examples use server-ip=127.0.0.1 to make Paper inaccessible outside the same machine's network environment. From another machine, a direct connection attempt to the backend's public address on port 25566 must fail while connecting to the proxy works.
article.serveropsaetning.text50: On separate machines or in separate containers, 127.0.0.1 does not point from the proxy to Paper. Use the backend's private address in the proxy's server list and bind Paper to the appropriate local interface. Restrict the backend port with a firewall to the proxy's source address, including IPv6. Do not allow regular players direct access to a backend with online-mode=false.
article.serveropsaetning.text51: If your hosting provider does not let you restrict access to a legacy backend, secure access before opening it, for example with BungeeGuard on both proxy and backend. Also see PaperMC's backend security guide.
article.serveropsaetning.text53: Java errors at startup: Check java -version and each JAR's requirements. A hosting panel may use a different Java version from the terminal.
article.serveropsaetning.text54: Address already in use: Two processes are trying to use the same port. The proxy uses 25565 and the Paper backend uses 25566; run only one of the two proxies.
article.serveropsaetning.text55: Connection refused or timeout: Start Paper, check the proxy's backend address and port, and inspect the firewall or container network.
article.serveropsaetning.text56: Forwarding or secret errors: Match modern forwarding and the secret on both sides for Velocity. Match ip_forward and settings.bungeecord for Waterfall. Restart both processes after making changes.
article.serveropsaetning.text57: Wrong skin or UUID: Check the proxy's online-mode and the entire forwarding setup before letting players continue. Incorrect UUIDs can lead to different player data and permissions.
article.serveropsaetning.text58: The setup is ready when login through the intended address works, the backend has the correct player identity and direct external backend access is blocked in proxy setups. To connect to MineClub, continue with registration and approval.

home.intro: Build, trade and compete across MineClub. Integrate payments and votes directly into your Paper server.
home.copyNote: Copy the address and add it under Multiplayer in Minecraft.
